answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 179 aliases as a result costs 242 bonds held for 12 days each, plus the vine attestations those aliases can never earn. A single prism checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a marble, before it can post or attest. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
